root_cause: The WPC bulletin parser passes coordinate tokens from valid feature lines directly into _decode_coords, which assumes the token is numeric apart from an optional leading minus. Historical CODSUS products sometimes contain embedded punctuation or stray letters inside otherwise valid coordinate tokens, so the parser can either fail during numeric conversion or lose otherwise parseable feature geometry instead of decoding the digits that remain.
approach: Keep the fix local to coordinate decoding by preserving the existing optional leading minus handling, then filtering the remaining coordinate token down to digits before the split and float conversion. Add a focused BytesIO regression test with a front line containing embedded punctuation and letters in coordinate fields, asserting the resulting LineString decodes from the remaining digits.
tests_to_add: Regression test that parse_wpc_surface_bulletin handles COLD/WARM coordinate tokens such as 411"45 and I4222 without raising
risk_notes: Filtering all non-digits may hide severely malformed tokens by producing a shorter but still parseable coordinate, so the regression should cover only otherwise valid historical archive corruption.
out_of_scope_observations: Malformed feature labels such as TRmOF being ignored or warned about is related parser ergonomics but should be handled separately from coordinate-token corruption.
